recipes.name: Mound Bars
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 ounce) package semisweet chocolate chips, melted

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine graham cracker crumbs, sugar, and melted butter in a bowl; mix to combine and pat into the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking pan. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Keep the oven on.
Combine condensed milk and flaked coconut; spread over the crust and continue to bake for 15 minutes.
Spread melted chocolate over coconut layer. Set aside to cool and let chocolate harden, about 1 hour. Cut into squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Mound Bars
raw_recipe.description: These mound bars have a rich coconut filling on a graham cracker crust topped with chocolate. If you're a fan of Mound candy bars — you're in for a treat!

review.reviewBody: I make these bars every year for Christmas as they are awesome. I agree that the coconut is hard to spread without breaking the graham cracker crust, but have found a simple solution. As soon as you pull them out of the oven after baking the coconut, I use the flat side of a spoon, sprayed with cooking spray and smooth out the coconut. The coconut mix is now more pliable, now that it is hot. I finish recipe as follows. I even sometimes sprinkle a few slivered almonds on top top make them like Alomnd Joys.

These are excellent with a little tweaking. I did not mix the cracker crumbs, sugar and butter, but rather melted the butter (I used a bit more than called for) in the pan in the oven, omitted the sugar completely, and just sprinkled the crumbs on top of the melted butter, pressed it down a bit, then let it bake. I almost doubled the coconut filling amount, using 3 1/2 cups of coconut (I chopped the flaked coconut in the processor to make it finer and more like real Mound Bars), sprinkled it atop the baked graham crust and poured 2 - 14 oz. cans of sweetened condensed milk over the coconut. Of course, it took much longer to bake (about 25 minutes). Once the filling set up, I just sprinkled the chocolate chips (tossed with about 1 1/2 Tbs. vegetable oil) evenly over it; put it back in the turned off oven and let the chips melt. I then spread the melted chocolate over all with an offset spatula (quite easy). I let it cool to room tempertature then refrigerated for about 2 hours before cutting into small bars (they cut very easily). They are absolutely delicious, especially with a hot cup of espresso.

Delicious! My family loves these. I used digestive biscuits for the crust because I happened to have some (that I didn't particularly like) on hand. Next time I'll omit the sugar from the crust -- I think that's a good idea, and I may use unsweetened coconut, to cut down on the sweetness. I warmed the coconut-condensed milk mixture slightly in the microwave to make it more spreadable. I added about 2 Tablespoons of butter to the chocolate, so it would be easier to cut once it cools. Next time I'll use Land O Lakes canola oil butter, which will likely soften the chocolate even further. I also used a pretty ceramic casserole dish that is about 8x12, as opposed to 9x13, so the bars are the perfect thickness. I'll definitely make these again. Yum!

I made these 2x. The first time I did follow the recipe for pan size, except I poured on the condensed milk & sprinkled the coconut on top & pressed in. I think it would be hard to spread mixture over the crust doing as directed. I also used mini chocolate chips as it covered more, there was barely anything to spread. The 2nd time I used 13 x 9 pan for a thicker cookie/candy. Baked the crust for 10 minutes, spread on the coconut, I stuck in a handful of slivered almonds sort of on top & pressed in with spoon & baked 18 min. more. I liked the thickness in a 13 x 9 & they were delicious. I spread 3/4 bag of a 12 oz. chocolate mini chips on top. You can easly used less when using mini chips, but I love my chocolate.....

I sprinkled the coconut on top of the crust after it baked, then I drizzled the sweetened condensed milk over the coconut. Then baked that for the last 15min. Also, for the chocolate topping, I used 6 regular sized Hershey's bars. I broke them up into individual squares and layed them on top of the coconut. Put in the oven for a minute, take a spoon & with the back of it spread the chocolate around. It comes out perfect every time! They are so good!!!

Honestly, I was pretty disappointed with the first round of this recipe. The crust was crumbly and never set properly. The coconut was impossible to spread, as was the chocolate. So here is how I did it on round two. I used no sugar and 1 cup of butter for 2 cups of graham crumbs. I sprinkled the coconut on top of the crust and then poured the condensed milk over that. I then sprinkled the chips on it and let it sit in the oven after I turned it off and then gently smoothed the top with a icing spatula. End of the day, this is a great concept for a recipe, but the directions as is are a little impractical.

I'd give these 5 stars, but they weren't quite as PRETTY as I wanted them to be. I lined a 9x9 glass pan with parchment paper, with edges extended, and patted the crust on top of the paper. Didn't use any sugar for the crust. Baked at 350 for 20 minutes (I think that was my problem; I should have baked them longer). Then I did what practically everyone else did and sprinkled the coconut on top of the hot base and drizzled the SCM on top of that. Bake another 20 minutes (again, I think I should have left them in the oven a little longer). I finely chopped up 12 ounces of 60% cacao bittersweet Ghiradelli bars, and scattered them over the top of the (very nicely browned) coconut top, put back in the oven for 1-1/2 minutes, then used an offset spatula to spread the chocolate around. Easy peasy! Let cool in the pan for 1/2 an hour, then lifted the paper out onto a rack to cool an hour. The chocolate hadn't set up at all, so I refrigerated another hour, then cut into bars. My problem at that point was that the crust kind of fell apart, and I don't think the coconut filling was quite done (it was pretty thick). In spite of that, these were DELICIOUS, and I'd definitely make again. Taking these to work tomorrow...we'll see how it goes.

This recipe is excellent! Super easy and delicious. I made a couple changes but only to how I put them together to make it even easier. Once I take the crust out of the oven I pour the sweetened condensed milk over the crust and gently spread that evenly, then sprinkle the coconut over that and gently pat down into the sweetened condensed milk. Bake. Take out of the oven a couple minutes early and sprinkle with chocolate chips (I like to do 50% milk chocolate and 50% semi sweet). Allow to cook for a few more minutes, take out of the oven and spread the chocolate chips evenly and cool before cutting. I use a slightly smaller pan than a 9x13 so the bars are a little thicker. Yum! A huge hit every time I make them.

This was delicious! I made it in an 8x11 pan. I didn't add sugar to the crust. I added extra coconut. Probably 3 cups instead of 2. I heated the sweetened condensed milk to make it easier to spread. I had to really restrain myself so I didn't eat the whole pan in one sitting! Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I made these for every special occasion. They are quick to make and taste divine! I made a few changes to save time and mess: I cut out the sugar completely as the condensed milk is sweet enough, I spread the condensed milk on first and then put the coconut on top, pushing it down a bit with a spatula. This way I didn't have to deal with the sticky mess of the milk and coconut and saved a bowl! :) Also I put a whole bag of chocolate chips on top after it comes out of the oven the second time and cover the whole thing with foil. When its cooled down a bit, I use a spatula to even out the chocolate as it has now melted beautifully! I've also tried this recipe with mint chocolate on top and it was also SO good! yum! Thank you so much for posting this recipe...yum!!!

This got rave reviews! I used a whole small bag of sweetened coconut and almost 2 whole cans of sweetened condensed milk. I followed recommendation of others and immediately out of oven put on coconut and then spread milk over the coconut. I also used Hershey bars smooth side facing up but needed more than 6 bars for the whole 9x13... Maybe 8 or 9. Then put it back in the oven to melt the chocolate just for few mins. Kept it in fridge and used hot knife to cut the bars. Awesome!
Perfect recipe and everyone loves it

These were a huge hit with my trivia team, and people followed up with me to get the recipe because they loved them so much. The only thing I will change next time is that I will leave the sugar out of the crust; they're sweet enough without it.
This is better then mounds bars!
I'm not a huge fan of coconut but my husband is. I found this recipe for him... they were SO good. I ate most of them

This recipe was great as written. To avoid the crust from breaking up when adding the coconut mixture, I just placed about 10 small dollops around the pan and then used a spoon sprayed with Pam to smooth it out. The second time I made instead of graham crackers, I used crushed almonds as one of my friends is gluten free. It too turned out great.
Only thing is crust almost burned. Oven at correct temp. Maybe bake for 12 min? Otherwise very good. I put about 3/4 cup chopped walnuts on the top too!

After reading the reviews, I used unsweetened coconut and added more than the 2 cups (probably 3, but I didn’t measure). I sprinkled it on the crust, then poured the sweetened condensed milk over it. Used most of the 12 oz. bag of semi-sweet chips and it is plenty of chocolate. I used a 9 x 13 pan, so the bars did come out thinner than the main photo. They were horrible to cut and get out of the pan! Very chewy to eat, but the flavor is delicious. Oh, and I did add chopped almonds so they really are Almond Joy Bars rather than Mounds. 😆
